newsitem.title: UK: Birmingham City FC to raise 7.5 mln stg in float.
newsitem.headline: Birmingham City FC to raise 7.5 mln stg in float.

text.p: English first division soccer team Birmingham City on Wednesday announced plans to raise 7.5 million stg in a flotation valuing the club at 25 million stg.
Shares will be issued at a placement price of 50p and the minimum application will be for 1,000 shares. First dealings will be on March 7.
The club has been owned by Sport Newspapers Limited since 1993. The owners will see their stake diluted from 84.2 percent to 58.9 percent after flotation.
The proceeds from the flotation will be used to re-develop the Railway Stand at the club's St Andrews stadium and carry out other ground improvements to a value of 3.5 million stg.
The balance will be available to strengthen the squad and as general working capital.
One of the best-supported clubs outside the premier league, Birmingham's only major honour came in 1963 when they won the League Cup.
The club, managed by former England international Trevor Francis, are in the lower reaches of the first division and were knocked out of the F.A. Cup last weekend by second division Wrexham.
